hypothesis: F42's cause is the RAM expert store's books after a GPU-bank prefill: the bank refill looked each routed expert up once per layer per prompt (~104 counted requests per layer vs ~1065 for the CPU union), so decode started with flat usage, id-ranked pins, 7-9 of 16 pins active and first-read recency, and missed +57% more experts in RAM in its first ~25 tokens. Commit c7f79815 makes the bank keep the CPU union's books (uncounted reads, a recency touch of each chunk's union before the refill, each member counted once after the chunk's GPU MoE). On the identical answer, decode after the bank prefill should then miss fewer experts early and be faster than on the unfixed tree, closing most of the gap to the CPU union, with prefill time unchanged

notes: Trial vs baseline median: +6.27% (FX 2.2641 vs OX 2.1305 tok/s; means 2.2375 vs 2.1203; Welch t = 3.86 on tok/s). CPU-union reference UX (the fixed tree with COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH_MIN=100000, same 3100 MiB reserve, not part of this record): median 2.3005 tok/s, so OX/UX = 0.9261 (F42 on this code line), FX/UX = 0.9842; the fix recovers 67% of the OX-UX gap (means; 79% by medians).

Robustness: the first round of samples ran slower in every arm (FX s1 2.1254, OX s1 2.0752, UX s1 2.2716 tok/s; seq 2-4 right after the warm-up). Without each arm's s1: FX 2.2656 / OX 2.1316 / UX 2.3006 tok/s (means), FX/OX 1.0629 (Welch t = 36.9), FX/UX 0.9848 (t = -9.7), recovered 79% of the OX-UX gap.

Decomposition, means over 5+5+5 samples (decode forwards 1-25 on the server), OX / FX / UX: wall 11.752 / 11.152 / 10.881 s, decode MoE 7.995 / 7.408 / 7.142 s, fetch_wait 2.748 / 2.184 / 1.941 s (recovered 70%), attach 3.706 / 3.685 / 3.662 s, RAM-store misses 1684 / 1244 / 1072 (recovered 72%), 20.96 / 15.49 / 13.35 GiB read from SSD, non-MoE 3.757 / 3.744 / 3.739 s.

RAM tier at decode start (probe v4_dec_res, read under the store mutex; medians over samples), OX / FX / UX: layer requests 104 / 1068 / 1065 per layer, active pins 7.88 / 11.95 / 16.00 of 16 per layer, pin usage median 1.0 / 9.0 / 9.0, residents with usage <= 1 100.0% / 9.1% / 3.1%, layers whose pins are ids 0..15 1 / 0 / 0, pins among the layer's 16 most-used residents 100% / 75% / 100% (usage ties count; every OX resident has usage 1); of the experts decode routes in forwards 1-25, 868 / 1254 / 1461 resident at decode start (of 2192 / 2192 / 2207); first forward 82 / 100 / 199 of 258.

What the fix leaves: the books now match the CPU union's, but residency does not fully (the commit's own caveat: the bank reads an expert once per layer per prompt, so a member the RAM cache evicted earlier in the layer is not read back as the CPU union reads it). Pins are ranked by usage yet only 11.9 of 16 per layer are resident at decode start (UX 16), and of the first decode forward's 258 routed experts 100 are in RAM (UX 199, OX 82): forwards 1-5 still miss 192 more experts than UX (38% of OX's excess recovered) and carry most of the remaining time gap, while forwards 6-10 recover 87% and forwards 11-24 run slightly faster than UX. Swapping routing and RAM sets, FX's decode routing against UX's decode-start RAM finds 1450 of its experts resident (its own RAM: 1254): residency, not routing, is what is left.

Prefill: TTFT median FX 82.26 s vs OX 82.09 s (ratio 1.0021; means +0.21 s, Welch t = 1.57, not significant): the bookkeeping costs at most a few tenths of a second of an 82 s prefill. UX's TTFT is 215.9 s (the CPU-union prefill PR #1 replaces).

Strictly one variable: OX and FX run the same probe patch (identical +/- lines) with the same server environment (sample.txt server_env, engine_environ.txt); the engine sources of 93b74183 and 4feb6d48 differ by exactly c7f79815's lines (checked by run_f42fix.sh's preflight: git diff of c/ without c/tests); the binaries differ only through that. The decode routing is identical in all 10 OX and FX samples (all 1,075 token-layers of forwards 1-25, probe v4_dec_layer), and so is the prefill's store traffic (4,468 reads, all misses, 59.7 GB): the fix changes only the store's books.
